title: AI banned for all students in Frederick County Public Schools
key_facts: Frederick County (Maryland) School Board voted 6-1 on Wednesday night to ban student use of AI from pre-K through 12th grade.
The board first considered limiting the ban to younger students, then extended it through high school.
Concerns include cheating and over-reliance on technology; the dissenter worried older students would be less ready for college.
The ban has exceptions for lessons about AI itself and for students with disabilities.
The district had begun piloting Google's Gemini for middle and high school students weeks earlier.
How the ban will be enforced is still being decided; some teachers are returning to paper-and-pencil work.
quote_evidence: The Frederick County School Board voted 6-1 Wednesday night to ban students from using artificial intelligence across all grade levels, from pre-K through 12th grade.
District officials clarified that the policy does not mean students will never be allowed to interact with AI.
why_it_matters_hint: One of the strictest student AI bans in the Washington region, reversing a Gemini pilot.
